tagline: Twenty suburban miles, named for a line on a map.
intro: From I-95 near Chester the Blue Route runs twenty miles north through the suburbs of Delaware County, past wooded stretches and over the Schuylkill, to the Turnpike at Plymouth Meeting. Billboards are barred along the whole of it.

The name comes off a 1958 location report whose map drew the choices in colors, and the blue line up the Crum Creek valley beat the red, the yellow and the green. Building it took decades of lawsuits with the towns in its path. The Philadelphia Inquirer called it the most costly, most bitterly opposed highway in Pennsylvania history, and the 1985 agreement held part of it to four lanes.

moments.title: Crum Creek
moments.text: From MacDade Boulevard the freeway narrows to a four-lane parkway and keeps Crum Creek company through Wallingford and Swarthmore, until the creek turns off northwest past US 1.

moments.title: The Radnor griffin
moments.text: At the US 30 interchange a stone cairn crowns a hill and a griffin of crushed stone lies on the slope, put there to recall Radnor's beginnings in the Welsh Tract.

moments.title: Pearl Harbor Memorial Bridge
moments.text: Past West Conshohocken one bridge carries the road over the Schuylkill River, two railroad lines and the Schuylkill River Trail at once.
